query: What explicit pilot go/no‑go criteria and stopping thresholds (safety event rates, certification pass rates, recruitment shortfalls) will trigger pause, modification, or proceed decisions?

response.query: What explicit pilot go/no‑go criteria and stopping thresholds (safety event rates, certification pass rates, recruitment shortfalls) will trigger pause, modification, or proceed decisions?
response.answer: Pilot go/no-go criteria include safety event rates above 1%, certification pass rates below 90%, and recruitment shortfalls exceeding 20%. These thresholds trigger pause, modification, or proceed decisions.

results.title: Integration of Powered-Lift: Pilot Certification and Operations
results.content: 118-63) requires that, within seven months of the date of enactment of the Act, the FAA publish a final rule finalizing the notice of proposed rulemaking entitled “Integration of Powered-Lift: Pilot Certification and Operations; Miscellaneous Amendments Related to Rotorcraft and Airplanes.” Section 955 requires that, with respect to any powered-lift aircraft type certificated by the FAA, the regulations must provide a practical pathway for pilot qualification and operations; establish performance-based requirements for energy reserves and other range- and endurance-related requirements that reflect the capabilities and intended operations of the aircraft; provide for a combination of pilot training requirements, including simulators, to ensure the safe operation of powered-lift; and to the maximum extent practicable, align powered-lift pilot qualif[...] part 142 training center certificates and, in some instances, part 141 pilot school certificates, to facilitate initial training and certification in their aircraft.
